\chapter{Complexity — DTIME}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.DTIME
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This module defines what it means for a finite multi-tape Turing machine over the
binary alphabet to decide a language within a time bound, introduces the deterministic
time classes $\mathrm{DTIME}(T)$ of languages decidable in time $c \cdot T$ for some
constant $c$, and proves two basic structural facts: monotonicity of
$\mathrm{DTIME}$ in the time bound, and emptiness of the class when the bound vanishes
at some input length.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Deciding a language within a time bound]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.DecidesInTime}
\label{Turing.FinTM.DecidesInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
Let $M$ be a finite multi-tape Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be a
language over $\{0,1\}$ (a set of finite binary strings), and let
$T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be a time bound. We say that $M$ \emph{decides $L$
within time $T$} if on every input string $x$ the machine halts within $T(|x|)$ steps
and produces the single-symbol output $1$ when $x \in L$ and $0$ when $x \notin L$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The deterministic time class $\mathrm{DTIME}(T)$]
\lean{Complexity.DTIME}
\label{Complexity.DTIME}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInTime}
For a time bound $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the class $\mathrm{DTIME}(T)$
consists of all languages $L$ over the binary alphabet for which there exist a
constant $c \in \mathbb{N}$ and a finite multi-tape Turing machine $M$ over the binary
alphabet such that on every input $x$ the machine $M$ halts within $c \cdot T(|x|)$
steps and outputs $1$ if $x \in L$ and $0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of $\mathrm{DTIME}$ in the time bound]
\lean{Complexity.DTIME.mono}
\label{Complexity.DTIME.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono}
\difficulty{2}
Let $T_1, T_2 : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be time bounds with $T_1(n) \le T_2(n)$ for
every $n$. Then $\mathrm{DTIME}(T_1) \subseteq \mathrm{DTIME}(T_2)$: every language
over the binary alphabet decided by some finite multi-tape machine within
$c \cdot T_1(n)$ steps on inputs of length $n$, for some constant $c$, is also decided
by such a machine within $c \cdot T_2(n)$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Vanishing time bounds give the empty class]
\lean{Complexity.DTIME_eq_empty_of_exists_zero}
\label{Complexity.DTIME_eq_empty_of_exists_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME, Turing.FinTM.not_computesInTime_zero}
\difficulty{3}
Let $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be a time bound with $T(n) = 0$ for at least one
input length $n$. Then $\mathrm{DTIME}(T) = \emptyset$: no language over the binary
alphabet is decidable by a finite multi-tape machine within $c \cdot T$ steps for any
constant $c$, because on an input of length $n$ the allotted budget is
$c \cdot T(n) = 0$ and no machine halts in zero steps.
\end{theorem}
